items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: when I first met J.R. he came to Albany to play a gig and I found out he was from Utica, but I didn’t hang out with him that much. You know in later years we hung out

ctx.x: I don’t know. They talk about the Texas Tenors, you know, and a certain sound indicative of certain areas. I never really heard those guys until I’d already been playing. I mean I knew Chuck Mangione and Sal, and I knew J.R. But I didn’t meet Sammy Noto until I’d been playing maybe ten, fifteen years, and I don’t ever remember meeting Don Menza — and I’m sure I’m leaving out some guys, I’m sure there’s some other great players around. But we never really hung together. I mean I was from Albany and I just, I never…
Yeah, why not? We’ll start it up anew. Was there competition, and is there still a lot of competition to get what work is out there?
